structure: Part 3, address list, search, paging, organisation scoping and expiry. Read in full: address/AddressController.java (list path claimed, plus the organisation check every operation runs), address/AddressService.java (list path and the create-time expiry stamp claimed), AddressRepository, AddressListQuery, AddressListQueryImpl, ListCriteria, RequestedListFilters, AddressPageResponse; the shared top-level classes OrganisationScope, OrganisationScopedListQuery, ListMatchCriteria, ListPaging, SearchTerms, RequestedListFilterSupport and ExpiryIndexes (claimed once here for addresses and transporters); configuration/AddressTtlConfig and MongoConfig; filter/IdentityHeaderFilter; src/main/resources/application.yml (TTL, environment and Mongo client settings); the tests ListCriteriaTest, ListMatchCriteriaTest, OrganisationScopeTest, ExpiryIndexesTest, PageTestSupport (a test helper, proves nothing), AddressTtlConfigTest, IdentityHeaderFilterTest, IntegrationBase (shared IT helpers, incl. the bad-request matcher and the index assertions), AddressListIT, AddressSearchIT, AddressScopingIT, AddressExpiryIT, AddressRepositoryIT, AddressIndexIT and MongoConfigIT; docs/openapi/addresses.yml get /organisation/{orgId}/addresses and AddressPageResponse and the security scheme; README sections Security and trust boundary, API overview (list parameters and wire conventions), Address expiry (non-prod only), Indexes, and the Design notes bullets in scope. To find what the slice references, Address.java's @CompoundIndex and GlobalExceptionHandler's BadRequestException and type-mismatch handlers were also grepped. Covered: the GET list endpoint (route, paging bounds and messages, response object, ordering, tombstone exclusion, page beyond last), the four filters (q fields and literal partial matching, countryCode, role, searchRole), how they combine (role ANDed, q/countryCode/searchRole ORed), filter tidying, unknown-role 400, the searchRole label design, the trusted organisation header (400s, 404, problem bodies verbatim, MDC, logging), the controller-level organisation check, organisation and ACTIVE scoping of every query in general terms, the trust boundary the service relies on, non-prod expiry (variables, defaults, both prod safeguards, start-up failures, TTL indexes on both collections, what the TTL monitor removes), the org_status_created index, and the Mongo client settings MongoConfig proves.

claims.statement: The address book lists an organisation's live addresses at GET /organisation/{orgId}/addresses, one page at a time.
claims.quote: @RequestMapping("/organisation/{orgId}/addresses") ... @GetMapping @Operation(operationId = "list-addresses", summary = "List the caller's live addresses (paginated, searchable)")

claims.statement: The list's page parameter is a 1-based page number that defaults to 1.
claims.quote: | `page` | 1-based page number (default `1`) |

claims.statement: A page less than 1 is refused with a 400 bad-request problem whose detail is "page must be 1 or greater".
claims.quote: if (page < 1) { throw new BadRequestException("page must be 1 or greater"); }
claims.note: The handler puts ex.getMessage() in the problem detail; the IT asserts the 400 shape, not the detail text.

claims.statement: The list's pageSize parameter runs from 1 to 100 and defaults to 25 when not supplied.
claims.quote: public static final int MIN_PAGE_SIZE = 1; public static final int MAX_PAGE_SIZE = 100; public static final int DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE = 25;

claims.statement: A pageSize outside 1 to 100 is refused with a 400 bad-request problem whose detail is "pageSize must be between 1 and 100"; it is never clamped to the bound.
claims.quote: throw new BadRequestException("pageSize must be between " + MIN_PAGE_SIZE + " and " + MAX_PAGE_SIZE);

claims.statement: A non-numeric page or pageSize is refused with a 400 bad-request problem with no errors map.
claims.quote: an out-of-range or non-numeric value for either is a 400 bad-request problem with no {@code errors} map

claims.statement: Every list 400 (paging, unknown role or search role, missing header) is application/problem+json with type https://api.cdp.defra.cloud/problems/bad-request, title "Bad Request", status 400 and no errors key.
claims.quote: jsonPath("$.type").value("https://api.cdp.defra.cloud/problems/bad-request"), jsonPath("$.title").value("Bad Request"), jsonPath("$.status").value(400), jsonPath("$.errors").doesNotExist()

claims.statement: A pageSize at either bound is served as requested: 1 gives one item a page and 100 gives every item on one page.
The list response is a top-level object with items, page, pageSize, totalItems and totalPages, all required, never a bare array.
claims.quote: List responses are a top-level object (`items`, `page`, `pageSize`, `totalItems`, `totalPages`), never a bare array.

claims.statement: The response's pageSize is the page size served: the requested one, else the default 25.
claims.quote: description = "Page size served: the requested one, else the default"

claims.statement: totalItems is the count of every matching live address across all pages, and totalPages the number of pages at the served page size.
claims.ref: AddressPageResponse.java:23-32; OrganisationScopedListQuery.java:44-45; AddressListIT list_shouldReturn8ItemsAcross4Pages_whenPageSizeIs8 (30 items, pageSize 8, totalPages 4)
claims.quote: description = "Total number of matching addresses" ... description = "Total number of pages"
claims.note: mechanism: the total is an exact count over the same query as the page.

claims.statement: Each item on a list page is a full address response; a listed item always has deleted false.
claims.quote: jsonPath("$.items[*].deleted", everyItem(is(false)))

claims.statement: The list is ordered newest first by creation time, with ties broken by id, newest first.
claims.quote: Sort.by(Sort.Direction.DESC, "createdAt").and(Sort.by(Sort.Direction.DESC, "id"))

claims.statement: The caller cannot choose the list's order: the API takes no sort parameter.
claims.quote: @RequestParam(defaultValue = "1") int page ... @RequestParam(required = false) Integer pageSize ... String q ... countryCodes ... roles ... searchRoles
claims.note: Inferred from the parameter list, which has page, pageSize, q, countryCode, role and searchRole only.

claims.statement: Pages are disjoint: page 2 holds the addresses after page 1, with no repeats.
claims.quote: page1Ids.retainAll(page2Ids); assertThat(page1Ids).isEmpty();

claims.statement: A page beyond the last is a 200 with empty items, carrying the requested page number and the real totals.
claims.quote: listAddresses("page", "3") .andExpect(status().isOk()) .andExpect(jsonPath("$.items").isEmpty()) .andExpect(jsonPath("$.page").value(3)) .andExpect(jsonPath("$.totalItems").value(30)) .andExpect(jsonPath("$.totalPages").value(2));

claims.statement: The list leaves out soft-deleted addresses (tombstones): only ACTIVE addresses are listed and counted.
claims.quote: One page of the organisation's {@code ACTIVE} addresses that match the criteria.

claims.statement: Soft-deleted addresses are left out of every search path too: a q search and a countryCode search both skip tombstones.
claims.quote: void countryCodeSearchExcludesSoftDeletedRows() ... void searchIsOrgScopedAndExcludesSoftDeletedForQueryPath()

claims.statement: The list returns only the caller's organisation's addresses; another organisation's addresses are never listed or counted.
claims.quote: jsonPath("$.items[*].organisationId", everyItem(is(ORGANISATION_ID)))

claims.statement: With no filters, the list returns every live address of the organisation, including addresses with no roles or an empty roles list.
claims.quote: Without it, every live address is listed

claims.statement: The q search term matches case-insensitively against name, addressLine1, addressLine2, townOrCity, county and postcode.
claims.ref: AddressListQueryImpl.java:18-19; ListMatchCriteria.java:19-22; README.md:139; AddressSearchIT partialWordSearchMatches* tests
claims.quote: List.of("name", "addressLine1", "addressLine2", "townOrCity", "county", "postcode")

claims.statement: The q search is a partial match: an address matches when the term appears anywhere in a searched field (for example "gree" finds "Green Farm", "iv2" finds a postcode starting IV2).
claims.quote: return ".*" + Pattern.quote(searchTerm) + ".*";

claims.statement: A multi-word q is matched as one phrase, so "green valley" finds "Green Valley Livestock Farm" and "GREEN la" finds address line 1 "Green Lane"; words are not matched separately or out of order.
claims.quote: listAddresses("q", "green valley") ... listAddresses("q", "GREEN la")
claims.note: That words are not matched separately is inferred from the whole term being quoted into one pattern; no test proves a reordered phrase misses.

claims.statement: The q term is taken literally, not as a regular expression: q ".*" matches nothing unless a field contains ".*".
claims.quote: listAddresses("q", ".*") .andExpect(status().isOk()) .andExpect(jsonPath("$.totalItems").value(0));

claims.statement: The q search term is trimmed, and an absent or all-whitespace q means no search.
claims.quote: searchTerm = searchTerm == null ? "" : searchTerm.trim();
claims.note: mechanism: tidies the q request parameter. That whitespace-only q lists everything is inferred from the trim and the isEmpty check; no test proves it.

claims.statement: The list sets no minimum or maximum length on q.
claims.quote: @RequestParam(required = false) String q,
claims.note: Inferred from the parameter's declaration and schema (type string, no bounds).

claims.statement: countryCode takes one or more ISO alpha-2 country codes as a repeated parameter, and on its own lists the addresses in any of them.
claims.quote: One or more ISO country codes (repeat the parameter). Alone, it lists the addresses in any of them.

claims.statement: countryCode is matched exactly against the address's stored 2-character code.
claims.quote: return Criteria.where("countryCode").in(countryCodes);
claims.note: Exact match means a lower-case code such as "fr" would not match a stored "FR" (inferred; no test).

claims.statement: The list does not validate a countryCode value: an unrecognised code is accepted and simply matches no address.
claims.quote: @RequestParam(name = "countryCode", required = false) List<String> countryCodes,
claims.note: Inferred: the parameter is a plain string list with no constraint, unlike role and searchRole which bind to the role enum.

claims.statement: Country codes in the list request are trimmed and blank values dropped.
claims.quote: country codes trimmed without blanks
claims.note: mechanism: tidies the countryCode request parameters.

claims.statement: role takes one or more roles as a repeated parameter and keeps only the addresses holding any of them.
claims.quote: Keeps only addresses holding any of these roles. Repeatable.

claims.statement: The role and searchRole values are PLACE_OF_ORIGIN, CONSIGNOR, PLACE_OF_DESTINATION, CONSIGNEE and IMPORTER.
claims.quote: `PLACE_OF_ORIGIN`, `CONSIGNOR`, `PLACE_OF_DESTINATION`, `CONSIGNEE` or `IMPORTER`

claims.statement: An address with no roles (missing or empty list) never matches a role filter.
claims.quote: an address with no roles never matches it

claims.statement: The role filter applies across every page: totals and paging count only the addresses holding the roles.
claims.quote: Lists only the addresses holding any of them, across every page.

claims.statement: An unknown role value is refused with a 400 bad-request problem with no errors map; TRANSPORTER is not an address role.
claims.quote: listAddresses("role", "CONSIGNOR", "role", "TRANSPORTER") .andExpect(badRequestProblemWithNoErrors());

claims.statement: Repeated role values and repeated searchRole values are collapsed to one each.
claims.quote: roles = RequestedListFilterSupport.presentElements(roles).distinct().toList();
claims.note: mechanism: tidies the role and searchRole request parameters.

claims.statement: searchRole takes one or more roles as a repeated parameter; an address holding any of them matches the search, and on its own it lists those addresses.
claims.quote: An address holding any of them matches the search, as one matching `q` or `countryCode` does (OR semantics). Alone, it lists the addresses holding any of them.

claims.statement: An unknown searchRole value is refused with a 400 bad-request problem with no errors map.
claims.quote: listAddresses("searchRole", "TRANSPORTER").andExpect(badRequestProblemWithNoErrors());

claims.statement: A blank searchRole value beside other search roles is ignored rather than refused.
claims.quote: listAddresses("searchRole", "CONSIGNOR", "searchRole", "") .andExpect(status().isOk()) .andExpect(jsonPath("$.totalItems").value(1))
claims.note: mechanism: a blank enum parameter binds as null and the null is dropped.

claims.statement: q, countryCode and searchRole combine with OR: an address matching the term, any of the country codes or any of the search roles is returned.
claims.quote: an address matches when the search term appears in a searched field, its stored `countryCode` is one of them **or** it holds a search role (OR semantics, not AND)

claims.statement: role narrows the search with AND: only addresses holding a kept role are returned from the matches of q, countryCode and searchRole.
claims.quote: It narrows the search (`q`, `countryCode` and `searchRole`)

claims.statement: searchRole is how a caller searches by a role's label: the caller works out which roles' labels contain the user's term and sends those roles, and the service matches stored roles.
claims.quote: A caller searches by role label through `searchRole`, naming the roles whose label contains the term, and the service matches stored roles.

claims.statement: The address book holds no role labels: it stores role enum names only, the labels are the caller's copy, and q never matches a role label such as "place of origin".
claims.quote: The labels are the caller's copy: the address book stores enum names and holds no labels, so matching a label here would make it a second owner of text in one language. A regular expression over the stored names would never match a label such as 'place of origin'.

claims.statement: A caller's grouping of roles, such as the INS address book's tabs, belongs to the caller, which lists a tab by sending its roles as repeated role values.
claims.quote: A caller's groupings of roles, such as the INS address book's tabs, are the caller's: it sends the roles a tab shows as repeated `role` values.

claims.statement: An absent list filter is treated as empty, never null, and null values inside a repeated parameter are dropped.
claims.quote: The filters of a list request. A filter the request did not supply is empty, never null.
claims.note: mechanism: normalises the list request's filters.

claims.statement: Inside the service, a search match must carry at least one value and a text match needs a pattern; an empty country or role match is refused with "A match needs at least one value".
claims.quote: throw new IllegalArgumentException("A match needs at least one value");
claims.note: mechanism: internal guard on the list criteria; no caller sees it, because the service adds a match only for a filter that has values (AddressService.java:86-99).

claims.statement: The list is one composed query whose filters are added only when the caller supplies them, always inside the organisation and ACTIVE scope.
claims.quote: The list is one composed query (`AddressListQuery`), not a fixed query per combination of search term, country code, roles and search roles.
claims.note: mechanism: builds the list query from the requested filters.

claims.statement: The list request is logged at info with page, pageSize, the country codes, roles and search roles, and only whether q was present, never the search term itself.
claims.quote: "GET addresses - page {}, pageSize {}, q present {}, countryCodes {}, roles {}," + " searchRoles {}"

claims.statement: Every request under /organisation/ must carry the trusted Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header, the sole tenant key for organisation-scoped reads and writes.
claims.quote: {@code Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id} is the sole tenant key for org-scoped reads and writes.

claims.statement: A missing or blank organisation header is refused with a 400 before any handler runs, with detail "Missing required header Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id", on every method (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE).
claims.quote: String detail = "Missing required header " + ORGANISATION_ID_HEADER;

claims.statement: A malformed organisation header (anything but 1 to 64 letters, digits, underscores or hyphens) is refused with a 400 whose detail is "Invalid Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id".
claims.quote: Pattern.compile("^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$") ... String detail = "Invalid " + ORGANISATION_ID_HEADER;

claims.statement: The header 400 is an application/problem+json body with type https://api.cdp.defra.cloud/problems/bad-request, title "Bad Request", status 400, the detail, the request's traceId when there is one, and no errors key; it is never a 401 or 403.
claims.quote: assertThat(body).containsEntry("title", "Bad Request"); ... assertThat(body).doesNotContainKey("errors"); assertThat(response.getStatus()).isNotIn(401, 403);

claims.statement: When the path orgId does not match the organisation header, the request is refused with a 404 before any handler runs, so another organisation's data is never disclosed.
claims.quote: Header value does not match path `{orgId}` → **404** (no cross-org existence disclosure)

claims.statement: The mismatch 404 body has type https://api.cdp.defra.cloud/problems/not-found, title "Resource Not Found", status 404 and detail "Resource not found".
claims.quote: NotFoundException.organisationMismatch(pathOrgId, organisationId, "Resource not found"); reject(response, HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, NOT_FOUND_TYPE, "Resource Not Found", refusal.detail(), refusal.getMessage());

claims.statement: A mismatched list, get, update, delete or create changes nothing: no address is soft-deleted and nothing is saved.
claims.quote: deleteAddressAs(ORG_A, ORG_B, id).andExpect(status().isNotFound()); assertThat(addressRepository.findByIdAndOrganisationId(id, ORG_A)) .get() .extracting("status") .isEqualTo(AddressStatus.ACTIVE); postAddressAs(ORG_A, ORG_B, addressBody()).andExpect(status().isNotFound()); assertThat(activeAddressesFor(ORG_A)).singleElement();

claims.statement: A create without the organisation header is a 400 and saves nothing.
claims.quote: postAddressAs(ORG_A, null, addressBody()).andExpect(badRequestProblemWithNoErrors()); assertThat(storedCount(Address.class)).isZero();

claims.statement: Every header refusal is logged once at warn as "Rejected /organisation request: <reason> (trace: <trace id>)"; a mismatch's reason names both organisation ids.
claims.quote: "Rejected /organisation request: Organisation mismatch: path orgId org-a is not the" + " caller's organisation org-b (trace: null)"

claims.statement: An accepted request carries the caller's organisation id in its logging context (organisationId) for its whole run, removed afterwards even when the request fails, and no address field values go into the logs.
claims.quote: MDC.put(MDC_ORGANISATION_ID, organisationId); chain.doFilter(request, response); } finally { MDC.remove(MDC_ORGANISATION_ID);

claims.statement: Requests outside /organisation/, such as /health, are not checked for the organisation header.
claims.quote: return !isOrganisationPath(organisationRequestPath(request));

claims.statement: The header check writes its own problem bodies and reads the request path from the servlet path, falling back to the request URI when a proxy leaves the servlet path empty.
claims.quote: `IdentityHeaderFilter` writes its own problem bodies, because `@RestControllerAdvice` does not handle exceptions thrown from servlet filters. It reads the path from `servletPath`, falling back to `requestURI` when a proxy or MockMvc leaves `servletPath` empty.
claims.note: mechanism: works out the request path for the organisation check.

claims.statement: Each address operation, list and create included, checks again that the path orgId matches the header and answers a mismatch with a 404 "Address not found", logged once at warn with the resource, its id and both organisation ids.
claims.quote: OrganisationScope.authorise(RESOURCE, null, orgId, organisationId, AddressService.ADDRESS_NOT_FOUND);
claims.note: The header filter refuses a mismatch first, so this check is a second line; a matching organisation passes silently (OrganisationScopeTest authorise_allowsAMatchingOrganisationSilently).

claims.statement: Every read and write of an address is scoped to the caller's organisation: the service offers no way to read, change or delete an address by id alone.
claims.quote: no code path reads or deletes another organisation's addresses by address id alone

claims.statement: The list query is always scoped to the organisation and to ACTIVE status, whichever filters the caller adds.
claims.quote: The list query is a custom repository fragment (`AddressListQuery`) that takes the organisation id and always scopes by it and by `ACTIVE` status.

claims.statement: An organisation browsing its own path cannot see or reach another organisation's address: its list is empty and get, update and delete of that id are 404.
claims.quote: listAddressesAs(ORG_B, ORG_B) .andExpect(status().isOk()) .andExpect(jsonPath("$.items").isEmpty()) ... getAddressAs(ORG_B, ORG_B, id).andExpect(status().isNotFound()); putAddressAs(ORG_B, ORG_B, id, addressBody()).andExpect(status().isNotFound()); deleteAddressAs(ORG_B, ORG_B, id).andExpect(status().isNotFound());

claims.statement: A 404 for another organisation's address has the same problem body as a 404 for an unknown id, and neither carries an instance field.
claims.quote: a cross-organisation request and an unknown id are deliberately indistinguishable, so the address book never confirms that another organisation holds a given id.

claims.statement: A cross-organisation get is logged with the address id and the caller's organisation id: "Address <id> not found in organisation <org>".
claims.quote: .endsWith("Address " + id + " not found in organisation " + ORG_B);

claims.statement: An address's organisation is taken from the header on create and scopes its later reads: it is listed and fetched only under that organisation.
claims.quote: assertThat(address.getOrganisationId()).isEqualTo(ORG_A)

claims.statement: The service has no authentication layer of its own: tenant isolation depends on the upstream hop authenticating the user, replacing the organisation header from the verified session, and network policy blocking direct access.
claims.quote: This service has **no Spring Security layer** and does not validate JWTs or API keys. Tenant isolation relies entirely on a trusted-forwarded-header contract
claims.note: Security finding, stated in general terms only. The README names the upstream owners as CDP ingress or the calling BFF (such as ins-frontend) and CDP network policy, and says adding a resource server was deferred.

claims.statement: The OpenAPI contract declares the organisation header as an apiKey security scheme that must match the path orgId, and the list's responses as 200, 400, 404 and 500.
claims.quote: description: Caller organisation id from the trusted forwarded header; must match path orgId

claims.statement: Outside prod, addresses are removed automatically a set number of days after they are created, so test data does not build up.
claims.quote: Outside prod, addresses are removed automatically a set number of days after they are created, so test data does not build up.

claims.statement: ADDRESS_TTL_DAYS sets how many days after creation an address expires; it is unset by default, which turns stamping off.
claims.ref: application.yml:26-28; README.md:356; AddressTtlConfig.java:26-28; AddressTtlConfigTest binding_leavesDaysUnsetWhenNotConfigured, binding_leavesDaysUnsetWhenConfiguredEmpty, binding_readsTheConfiguredDays
claims.quote: | `ADDRESS_TTL_DAYS` | unset | Days after creation an address expires.

claims.statement: ADDRESS_TTL_DAYS must be positive when set: zero or a negative value stops the service starting.
claims.quote: Must be positive when set, so a misconfiguration fails at startup rather than stamping an already-elapsed {@code expireAt}

claims.statement: ADDRESS_TTL_EXPIRY_ENABLED, false by default, turns on the MongoDB TTL index that removes expired documents.
claims.ref: application.yml:30-31; README.md:357; ExpiryIndexes.java:32; ExpiryIndexesTest bean_isAbsentWhenExpiryIsNotConfigured, bean_isAbsentWhenExpiryIsDisabled, bean_existsWhenExpiryIsEnabled
claims.quote: | `ADDRESS_TTL_EXPIRY_ENABLED` | `false` | When `true`, the `address_expire_at_ttl` MongoDB TTL index is created at startup and MongoDB removes documents once `expireAt` has passed

claims.statement: ENVIRONMENT names the running environment (default local); prod is "prod" in any case, ignoring surrounding whitespace.
claims.quote: return environment != null && "prod".equalsIgnoreCase(environment.strip());

claims.statement: A missing or blank ENVIRONMENT stops the service starting, rather than being read as non-prod.
claims.quote: `ENVIRONMENT` must not be blank — the service fails to start if it is.

claims.statement: First prod safeguard: a new address gets an expiry date only when ADDRESS_TTL_DAYS is set and ENVIRONMENT is not prod.
claims.quote: `expireAt` is only set when `ADDRESS_TTL_DAYS` is configured **and** `ENVIRONMENT` is not `prod`.

claims.statement: Second prod safeguard: the TTL indexes are created only when ADDRESS_TTL_EXPIRY_ENABLED is true and ENVIRONMENT is not prod; in prod the service logs a warning and creates none.
claims.quote: log.warn("Expiry is enabled in prod; refusing to create the address and transporter TTL indexes");

claims.statement: A new address's expiry date is the moment of creation plus ADDRESS_TTL_DAYS days.
claims.quote: address.setExpireAt(Instant.now().plus(days, ChronoUnit.DAYS));
claims.note: Counted from the moment of creation rather than createdAt, which auditing fills during the save (README.md:387).

claims.statement: The expiry date is internal: it is not returned on the wire.
claims.quote: .andExpect(jsonPath("$.expireAt").doesNotExist());

claims.statement: Updating or soft-deleting an address keeps its original expiry date.
claims.quote: Updates and deletes keep the original `expireAt`.

claims.statement: The TTL index address_expire_at_ttl is on expireAt with zero seconds' delay, so MongoDB removes an address once its expiry date has passed.
claims.quote: new Index().on("expireAt", Sort.Direction.ASC).expire(Duration.ZERO).named(indexName)

claims.statement: The same expiry switch creates a transporter TTL index, transporter_expire_at_ttl, on the transporters' expireAt.
claims.quote: static final String TRANSPORTER_INDEX_NAME = "transporter_expire_at_ttl";
claims.note: Shared expiry class, claimed here once for both records.

claims.statement: The TTL indexes are created when the application is ready at start-up.
claims.quote: @EventListener(ApplicationReadyEvent.class) public void createIndexes()

claims.statement: Expiry removes active addresses and tombstones alike once their expiry date has passed.
claims.quote: MongoDB removes documents once `expireAt` has passed — active addresses and tombstones alike.

claims.statement: An address with no expiry date, such as one created before expiry was switched on, is never removed by expiry; one whose date has not passed stays.
claims.quote: Mongo's TTL monitor skips documents with no date in {@code expireAt}, so addresses and transporters created before expiry was switched on are never removed by it.

claims.statement: Switching expiry off again does not drop a TTL index that already exists.
claims.quote: Switching the flag back off does not drop an index that already exists.

claims.statement: The TTL indexes are created explicitly rather than declared on the field, so automatic index creation never builds them in prod.
claims.quote: Created here rather than with {@code @Indexed(expireAfter)} on the field because {@code auto-index-creation} would then build it in every environment, prod included.

claims.statement: The list is served by the org_status_created compound index on organisationId ascending, status ascending and createdAt descending.
claims.quote: @CompoundIndex(name = "org_status_created", def = "{'organisationId': 1, 'status': 1, 'createdAt': -1}")

claims.statement: The addresses collection declares no index besides _id and org_status_created, and the list query's plan uses org_status_created with no collection scan.
claims.quote: .containsExactlyInAnyOrder("_id_", "org_status_created"); ... assertThat(winningPlan.toJson()).doesNotContain("COLLSCAN");
claims.note: The TTL index is dropped after AddressExpiryIT, so the index-only assertion holds when expiry is off.

claims.statement: An address book is expected to hold tens to hundreds of addresses, so a bounded scan is acceptable and any further index waits on real collection sizes.
claims.quote: Datasets are one user's address book today (tens to hundreds of rows), so a bounded scan is acceptable. Reassess any future index against real collection size before adding it.

claims.statement: The org_status_created index was created while the collection was empty, so no later index build runs on a populated collection.
claims.quote: The `org_status_created` index was created while the collection was empty, so no later index build runs on a populated collection.

claims.statement: The service reads from MongoDB with primaryPreferred read preference, so a read straight after a write sees that write.
claims.quote: // UI is POST/redirect/GET; secondary reads break read-your-writes, so the // default is overridden from the template's `secondary` to `primaryPreferred`.

claims.statement: The service writes to MongoDB with majority write concern.
claims.quote: write-concern: ${MONGO_WRITE_CONCERN:majority}

claims.statement: The service's MongoDB database is trade-imports-address-book by default, reached over TLS with the CDP truststore certificates.
claims.quote: database: ${MONGO_DATABASE:trade-imports-address-book}

claims.statement: The MongoDB connection pool holds 10 to 100 connections by default, waits up to 2 seconds for one and closes one idle for 60 seconds.
claims.quote: min-size: ${MONGO_POOL_MIN_SIZE:10} max-size: ${MONGO_POOL_MAX_SIZE:100} max-wait-time-ms: ${MONGO_POOL_MAX_WAIT_TIME_MS:2000} max-connection-idle-time-ms: ${MONGO_POOL_MAX_IDLE_TIME_MS:60000}
